science.label: Sector 20
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 17.5 hours, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 20 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.95%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.29%, the light's own noise being 0.16%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 0.73 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.22, a width of 0.50 and a fit of 0.99, and in all 12 of the star's sectors together a period of 0.73 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.32, a width of 0.48 and a fit of 0.99; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random. Gaia DR3 lists 6 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 2.0% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffd486, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 60 (December 2022 and January 2023): the map's scale, 99.4% to 100.6% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 1.2% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · December 2022 and January 2023
